chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who partook of the pre-dawn meal, then went out from his house, and the dawn had emerged and was clear. He (peace be upon him) said:
He should complete that fast of his, then let him make it up. So, if he partook of the pre-dawn meal during other than the month of Ramadan after the dawn, he should break (his fast).

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father was praying one night, and I was eating. So he finished and said: As for Ja'far, he has eaten and drunk after the dawn.' So he instructed me, so I broke the fast of that day, which was other than the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one eats after dawn has clearly emerged during Ramadan versus other months?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between *shubha* (doubt) and *yaqin* (certainty) regarding dawn, establishing that eating after clear dawn emergence invalidates the fast only outside Ramadan, whereas in Ramadan it requires completion and makeup. The narrative highlights the practical application of this ruling within the Ahl al-Bayt household, illustrating how Imam al-Sadiq (AS) applied specific jurisprudential nuances to daily life. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing of *al-fajr al-sadiq* (true dawn) as the threshold for fasting validity.
